citation: J.-M. Muller, N. Brunie, F. de Dinechin, C.-P. Jeannerod, M. Joldes, V. Lefevre, G. Melquiond, N. Revol, S. Torres, "Handbook of Floating-Point Arithmetic", 2nd ed., Birkhauser, 2018

segments.title: 1 Introduction
segments.why: The chapter is introductory/history material without arithmetic-unit design detail.

segments.title: 2 Definitions and Basic Notions
segments.why: The chapter defines floating-point numbers/rounding properties rather than hardware mechanisms.

segments.title: 3 Floating-Point Formats and Environment
segments.why: The chapter specifies floating-point formats/environment semantics rather than arithmetic-unit implementations.

segments.title: 4 Basic Properties and Algorithms
segments.why: The chapter presents numerical/software algorithms and floating-point properties without a hardware mechanism.

segments.title: 5 Enhanced Floating-Point Sums, Dot Products,and Polynomial Values
segments.why: The chapter develops compensated numerical algorithms for sums/dot products/polynomials and defers hardware acceleration to Chapter 8.

segments.title: 6 Languages and Compilers
segments.why: The chapter concerns programming languages/compilers rather than arithmetic-unit microarchitecture.

segments.title: 7 Algorithms for the Basic Operations
segments.why: The chapter defines implementation algorithms and correct-rounding structures for binary/decimal addition, multiplication, division, square root, and FMA.

segments.title: 8 Hardware Implementation of Floating-Point Arithmetic
segments.why: The chapter reviews fixed-point primitives and evaluates complete hardware datapaths for floating-point add/multiply/divide/square-root/FMA and enhanced sum/dot operations.

segments.title: 9 Software Implementation of Floating-Point Arithmetic
segments.why: The chapter explicitly implements floating-point operations as software on integer processors.

segments.title: 10 Evaluating Floating-Point Elementary Functions
segments.why: The chapter surveys hardware-relevant LUT/polynomial/shift-add/range-reduction mechanisms and correct-rounding strategies for elementary functions.

segments.title: 11 Complex Numbers
segments.why: The chapter presents numerical algorithms for complex arithmetic without arithmetic-unit microarchitecture.

segments.title: 12 Interval Arithmetic
segments.why: The chapter concerns interval-arithmetic semantics and numerical error bounds rather than hardware mechanisms.

segments.title: 13 Verifying Floating-Point Algorithms
segments.why: The chapter concerns formal verification of floating-point algorithms rather than arithmetic-unit designs.

segments.title: 14 Extending the Precision
segments.why: The chapter describes software techniques for extended/multiple precision rather than a covered hardware-unit mechanism.

segments.title: A.1 Continued Fractions
segments.why: The appendix supplies number-theory tools for approximation/range-reduction proofs without hardware design detail.

segments.title: A.2 Euclidean Lattices
segments.why: The appendix presents Euclidean-lattice theory for approximation/search problems rather than arithmetic-unit mechanisms.

segments.title: B.1 The IEEE 754-1985 Standard
segments.why: The appendix summarizes a superseded floating-point standard and contains no microarchitectural design detail.

segments.title: B.2 The IEEE 854-1987 Standard
segments.why: The appendix summarizes IEEE 854 format/operation requirements rather than implementation mechanisms.

segments.title: B.3 The Need for a Revision
segments.why: The appendix gives historical motivation for standards revision without arithmetic-unit design detail.

segments.title: B.4 The IEEE 754-2008 Revision
segments.why: The section is standards history followed by bibliography/back matter rather than a mechanism chapter.
